text:
maya: alert from the dashboard: eu-west1c eviction rate jumped and a bunch of tiny GPU pods are bouncing between nodes
oliver: saw that, looks like a binpack churn. small 1-GPU jobs arrive, scheduler packs them, then larger gang jobs force consolidation and evict the small ones
maya: quick `kubectl` check shows inconsistent `nvidia-topo` labels across newly provisioned nodes
cheng: run the probe we use:
```
kubectl get nodes -l zone=eu-west1c -o custom-columns=NODE:.metadata.name,IMG:.spec.providerID,TOPO:.metadata.labels.nvidia-topo --no-headers
```
infra-oncall: sample output:
```
gpu-eu-01  gce://projects/redwood-gpu/ami-stable      nvlink
gpu-eu-02  gce://projects/redwood-gpu/ami-stable      nvlink
gpu-eu-03  gce://projects/redwood-gpu/ami-fallback    none
gpu-eu-04  gce://projects/redwood-gpu/ami-fallback    none
```
oliver: autoscaler probably used fallback AMI during a fast scale-up when the image mirror timed out; fallback AMI doesn't have the nvlink label applied at boot
cheng: that mismatch makes the scheduler place tiny pods on the fallback nodes. Later, when a gang needing nvlink appears, we evict and reschedule -> repack spiral
descheduler-bot: descheduler canary triggered compaction in eu-west1c 2m ago
maya: immediate actions:
- cordon the AMI-fallback nodes
- drain tiny jobs into warmpool to stop immediate churn
- pause descheduler canary in the AZ
- reprovision nodes with baked image that sets `nvidia-topo=nvlink` at boot
oliver: doing cordon+drain now: `kubectl cordon gpu-eu-03 && kubectl drain gpu-eu-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data`
infra-oncall: cordon/drain started, moving ~10 pods; ETA ~4m
cheng: medium term changes:
- scheduler: add a soft topology preference for `nvidia-topo=nvlink` with a 120s grace before compaction evictions for <2m pods
- scheduler scoring: reduce packing weight for short-lived pods (multiplier 0.2) so they don't trigger aggressive compaction
- autoscaler: pin provisioner to AMI IDs (avoid tag drift) and add a preflight to validate node labels after boot
maya: creating INF ticket with node list, `kubectl describe` output, and deploy window. tagging infra-image and autoscaler teams
oliver: cost impact: churn caused ~1.7 extra node-hours in the hour window; we'll include that in the ticket
cheng: I'll open a small PR for the soft-pref + tiny-job weight and add an e2e sim that simulates mixed AMI boots to avoid regressions
descheduler-bot: descheduler canary paused in eu-west1c for 30m as requested
infra-oncall: after reprovision we'll run label parity check and rejoin nodes to the pool
maya: thanks team. keeping thread open until nodes are back to green :thumbsup:
